questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the neutral 18-electron organometallic complex $[(\eta^x\text{-C}_7\text{H}_7)\text{Mo}(\text{CO})_2\text{I}]$ (atomic number of $\text{Mo} = 42$), the hapticity $\eta^x$ of the $\text{C}_7\text{H}_7$ ring is
questions.explanationEn: Using the neutral-ligand counting method: $\text{Mo}$ (Group 6) contributes $6\text{ e}^-$, two $\text{CO}$ ligands contribute $2 \times 2 = 4\text{ e}^-$, and $\text{I}$ contributes $1\text{ e}^-$, giving $11\text{ e}^-$. To satisfy the 18-electron rule, the $\text{C}_7\text{H}_7$ ligand must contribute $18 - 11 = 7\text{ e}^-$, which corresponds to $\eta^7$ coordination (tropylium ligand).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes a Fischer carbene complex from a Schrock carbene (alkylidene) complex?
optionsEn: The carbene carbon is nucleophilic in Fischer carbenes and electrophilic in Schrock carbenes
Schrock carbenes require at least one heteroatom substituent ($-\text{OR}$ or $-\text{NR}_2$) directly bonded to the carbene carbon
The carbene carbon is electrophilic in Fischer carbenes (low-valent late metal, $\pi$-acceptor co-ligands) and nucleophilic in Schrock carbenes (high-valent early metal, $\pi$-donor/alkyl ligands)
Fischer carbenes always involve high-valent early transition metals in $d^0$ configurations
questions.explanationEn: Fischer carbenes (e.g., $[(\text{CO})_5\text{W}=\text{C(OMe)Ph}]$) feature low-valent mid-to-late transition metals with $\pi$-acceptor co-ligands and heteroatom-stabilized, electrophilic carbene carbons. Schrock carbenes (e.g., $[\text{Cp}_2\text{Ta}(\text{Me})(=\text{CH}_2)]$) feature high-valent early transition metals with alkyl/Cp ligands and H/alkyl-substituted, nucleophilic carbene carbons.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the industrial carbonylation of methanol to acetic acid, the Cativa process replaces the rhodium catalyst $[\text{Rh}(\text{CO})_2\text{I}_2]^-$ (Monsanto process) with an iridium catalyst $[\text{Ir}(\text{CO})_2\text{I}_2]^-$. The rate-determining step in the Monsanto (Rh) process and the Cativa (Ir) process are, respectively,
optionsEn: reductive elimination of $\text{CH}_3\text{COI}$ in both processes
migratory insertion of $\text{CO}$ (Monsanto) and oxidative addition of $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ (Cativa)
oxidative addition of $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ (Monsanto) and migratory insertion of $\text{CO}$ (Cativa)
hydrolysis of $\text{CH}_3\text{COI}$ in both processes
questions.explanationEn: In the Monsanto process, nucleophilic oxidative addition of $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ to $[\text{Rh}(\text{CO})_2\text{I}_2]^-$ is rate-determining. Because $5d$ $\text{Ir(I)}$ is much more nucleophilic than $4d$ $\text{Rh(I)}$, oxidative addition of $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ is $\sim 150\times$ faster in the Cativa process, shifting the rate-determining step to migratory insertion of $\text{CO}$ into the strong $\text{Ir}-\text{CH}_3$ bond.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In adenosylcobalamin (coenzyme $\text{B}_{12}$), the central cobalt atom is coordinated to a tetrapyrrolic corrin ring and an axial $5'$-deoxyadenosyl carbon ligand. The key initial chemical step in coenzyme $\text{B}_{12}$-dependent isomerase reactions is
optionsEn: homolytic cleavage of the weak $\text{Co(III)}-\text{C}$ bond to generate low-spin $\text{Co(II)}$ ($d^7$) and a $5'$-deoxyadenosyl carbon radical
heterolytic cleavage of the $\text{Co}-\text{C}$ bond to generate $\text{Co(I)}$ and an adenosyl carbocation
oxidative addition of $\text{O}_2$ to form a $\text{Co(V)}=\text{O}$ oxo intermediate
hydrolysis of the corrin ring amide side chains
questions.explanationEn: Adenosylcobalamin is a unique biological organometallic compound containing a weak $\text{Co(III)}-\text{C}$ bond ($\text{BDE} \approx 110\text{--}130\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$). Substrate binding triggers homolytic $\text{Co}-\text{C}$ cleavage to produce paramagnetic $\text{Co(II)}$ (cob(II)alamin) and a $5'$-deoxyadenosyl radical ($\text{AdoCH}_2^\bullet$), which abstracts an H atom from the substrate to initiate radical rearrangement.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Carboxypeptidase A is a zinc metalloenzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of the C-terminal peptide bond of proteins. Its active-site $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ ion is coordinated by
optionsEn: two histidine nitrogens, one bidentate glutamate carboxylate, and one water molecule
a heme protoporphyrin IX ring and a proximal histidine
three histidine nitrogens and one methionine sulfur
four cysteine thiolate sulfurs in a tetrahedral array
questions.explanationEn: In resting carboxypeptidase A, $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ is coordinated by two histidine imidazoles (His69, His196), one bidentate glutamate carboxylate (Glu72), and one water molecule (which is activated by $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ and general base Glu270 to attack the scissile peptide carbonyl).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn:
Which of the following mononuclear organometallic complexes obey the $18$-electron rule?
(Atomic numbers: $\text{Cr} = 24$, $\text{Mn} = 25$, $\text{Fe} = 26$, $\text{Co} = 27$, $\text{Ir} = 77$)
optionsEn: $[(\eta^6\text{-C}_6\text{H}_6)\text{Cr}(\text{CO})_3]$
$[(\eta^5\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5)\text{Mn}(\text{CO})_3]$
$[\text{IrCl}(\text{CO})(\text{PPh}_3)_2]$
$[\text{Fe}(\eta^4\text{-C}_4\text{H}_6)(\text{CO})_3]$
questions.explanationEn: Counting total valence electrons (neutral method): (A) $\text{Cr}(6) + \eta^6\text{-C}_6\text{H}_6(6) + 3\text{CO}(6) = 18\text{ e}^-$ (Obeys). (B) $\text{Mn}(7) + \eta^5\text{-Cp}(5) + 3\text{CO}(6) = 18\text{ e}^-$ (Obeys). (C) Vaska's complex: $\text{Ir}(9) + \text{Cl}(1) + \text{CO}(2) + 2\text{PPh}_3(4) = 16\text{ e}^-$ (Does not obey). (D) $\text{Fe}(8) + \eta^4\text{-butadiene}(4) + 3\text{CO}(6) = 18\text{ e}^-$ (Obeys). Hence (A), (B), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about iron-sulfur ($\text{Fe}-\text{S}$) electron-transfer proteins are CORRECT?
optionsEn: In all $\text{Fe}-\text{S}$ proteins (rubredoxin, $[2\text{Fe}-2\text{S}]$, and $[4\text{Fe}-4\text{S}]$ ferredoxins), every iron atom is tetrahedrally coordinated by sulfur atoms in a high-spin state
The oxidized $[2\text{Fe}-2\text{S}]^{2+}$ ferredoxin contains two high-spin $\text{Fe(III)}$ ions that are antiferromagnetically coupled to give a diamagnetic ($S = 0$) ground state

High-potential iron-sulfur proteins (HiPIP) cycle between $[4\text{Fe}-4\text{S}]^{3+}$ and $[4\text{Fe}-4\text{S}]^{2+}$, whereas bacterial ferredoxins cycle between $[4\text{Fe}-4\text{S}]^{2+}$ and $[4\text{Fe}-4\text{S}]^{+}$
Rubredoxin undergoes a two-electron transfer per iron center during biological redox cycling
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: weak-field tetrahedral sulfur coordination keeps every Fe center high-spin ($\text{Fe}^{3+}$ $S=5/2$ or $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ $S=2$). (B) True: superexchange through the two $\mu_2\text{-S}^{2-}$ bridges couples the two $S=5/2$ $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ spins antiparallel, giving $S_{\text{total}} = 0$ (EPR-silent). (C) True: HiPIP uses the $3+/2+$ couple ($E^\circ \approx +0.35\text{ V}$), while $[4\text{Fe}-4\text{S}]$ ferredoxins use the $2+/1+$ couple ($E^\circ \approx -0.40\text{ V}$). (D) False: rubredoxin is strictly a one-electron transfer protein ($\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}$). Hence (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total valence electron count of the active Cativa catalyst $[\text{Ir}(\text{CO})_2\text{I}_2]^-$ (atomic number of $\text{Ir} = 77$) is _______ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Using the neutral-ligand method: $\text{Ir}$ (Group 9) $= 9\text{ e}^-$, two $\text{CO}$ ligands $= 2 \times 2 = 4\text{ e}^-$, two $\text{I}$ ligands $= 2 \times 1 = 2\text{ e}^-$, and $-1$ charge $= +1\text{ e}^-$. Total valence electrons $= 9 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 16\text{ e}^-$ (square planar $d^8$ $\text{Ir(I)}$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: According to Wade-Mingos rules, the number of polyhedral skeletal electron pairs (SEPs) in the octahedral cluster $\text{Rh}_6(\text{CO})_{16}$ (atomic number of $\text{Rh} = 45$) is _______ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: For $\text{Rh}_6(\text{CO})_{16}$ ($n = 6$, $\text{Rh}$ is Group 9), total valence electrons $= 6(9) + 16(2) = 54 + 32 = 86\text{ e}^-$. Subtracting $12n = 72$ non-skeletal electrons gives $86 - 72 = 14$ skeletal electrons, which equals $\frac{14}{2} = 7$ skeletal electron pairs ($n + 1 = 7$, *closo* octahedron).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the thorium radioactive decay series $^{232}_{90}\text{Th} \longrightarrow {}^{208}_{82}\text{Pb}$, the number of $\alpha$-particles emitted is _______ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Only $\alpha$-emission ($^4_2\text{He}$) changes the mass number $A$ (each $\alpha$-particle reduces $A$ by $4$, whereas $\beta$-decay leaves $A$ unchanged). Therefore, $n_\alpha = \frac{232 - 208}{4} = \frac{24}{4} = 6$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the series of octahedral complexes $[\text{Mo}(\text{CO})_5\text{L}]$ where $\text{L} = \text{PF}_3, \text{P(OMe)}_3, \text{PPh}_3, \text{PMe}_3$, the $A_1$ carbonyl stretching frequency $\nu_{\text{CO}}$ decreases in the order
optionsEn: $\text{PF}_3 > \text{P(OMe)}_3 > \text{PPh}_3 > \text{PMe}_3$
$\text{PPh}_3 > \text{PMe}_3 > \text{PF}_3 > \text{P(OMe)}_3$
$\text{PMe}_3 > \text{PPh}_3 > \text{P(OMe)}_3 > \text{PF}_3$
$\text{PF}_3 > \text{PPh}_3 > \text{P(OMe)}_3 > \text{PMe}_3$
questions.explanationEn: As the substituents on phosphorus become more electronegative ($\text{Me} < \text{Ph} < \text{OMe} < \text{F}$), $\sigma$-donation decreases and $\pi$-acceptor ability increases ($\text{PMe}_3 < \text{PPh}_3 < \text{P(OMe)}_3 < \text{PF}_3$). Stronger $\pi$-acceptors compete with $\text{CO}$ for $\text{Mo}$ $d$-electron density, decreasing $\text{Mo} \to \text{CO}$ backbonding and raising $\nu_{\text{CO}}$. Thus $\nu_{\text{CO}}$ decreases in the order $\text{PF}_3 > \text{P(OMe)}_3 > \text{PPh}_3 > \text{PMe}_3$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Two-electron reduction of the neutral cluster $\text{Os}_6(\text{CO})_{18}$ with $\text{Na}/\text{Hg}$ produces the dianion $[\text{Os}_6(\text{CO})_{18}]^{2-}$. According to Wade-Mingos rules, the polyhedral metal-core geometry changes from
optionsEn: pentagonal pyramid (*nido*, $8$ SEPs) to butterfly (*arachno*, $9$ SEPs)
regular octahedron (*closo*, $7$ SEPs) to pentagonal pyramid (*nido*, $8$ SEPs)
bicapped tetrahedron (capped *closo*, $n$ SEPs $= 6$) to regular octahedron (*closo*, $n + 1$ SEPs $= 7$)
trigonal prism to bicapped tetrahedron
questions.explanationEn: For $\text{Os}_6(\text{CO})_{18}$ ($n = 6$): $\text{TVE} = 6(8) + 18(2) = 84\text{ e}^-$, giving $\text{PSE} = 84 - 12(6) = 12$ ($6$ SEPs $= n$). Since a $6$-vertex cluster has only $n = 6$ SEPs (instead of $n+1 = 7$), it adopts a **monocapped trigonal bipyramid / bicapped tetrahedron** (specifically bicapped tetrahedron for $\text{Os}_6(\text{CO})_{18}$). Adding $2\text{ e}^-$ to form $[\text{Os}_6(\text{CO})_{18}]^{2-}$ gives $\text{TVE} = 86\text{ e}^-$ and $7$ SEPs ($n + 1$), rearranging cleanly to a regular **octahedron** (*closo*).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: When 4-vinylcyclohex-1-ene is hydrogenated with $1\text{ equiv.}$ of $\text{H}_2$ in the presence of Wilkinson's catalyst, $[\text{RhCl}(\text{PPh}_3)_3]$, the major product is 4-ethylcyclohex-1-ene (selective reduction of the terminal exocyclic alkene) because
optionsEn: Wilkinson's catalyst operates only on acyclic alkenes and cannot bind cyclic alkenes
the terminal alkene reacts via a free-radical mechanism

sterically bulky $\text{PPh}_3$ ligands on the active $14$-electron $[\text{RhCl}(\text{PPh}_3)_2]$ species strongly favor coordination and insertion of the less hindered monosubstituted terminal alkene over the internal disubstituted alkene
the internal cyclohexene double bond is electronically too electron-rich to bind $\text{Rh(I)}$
questions.explanationEn: Wilkinson's catalyst dissociates one bulky $\text{PPh}_3$ to form $[\text{RhCl}(\text{PPh}_3)_2]$ (which oxidatively adds $\text{H}_2$ to $[\text{RhH}_2\text{Cl}(\text{PPh}_3)_2]$). Because two bulky $\text{PPh}_3$ ligands remain coordinated, alkene binding and migratory insertion are governed strongly by steric accessibility: monosubstituted terminal alkenes react much faster than disubstituted internal alkenes.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Simple synthetic iron(II) porphyrins in solution are irreversibly oxidized by $\text{O}_2$ to the $\mu$-oxo dimer $[(\text{Por})\text{Fe}^{\text{III}}-\text{O}-\text{Fe}^{\text{III}}(\text{Por})]$. Collman's 'picket-fence porphyrin' achieves reversible $\text{O}_2$ binding at room temperature by
optionsEn: replacing iron with ruthenium so that $\text{O}_2$ cannot oxidize the metal
attaching four negatively charged sulfonate groups to repel $\text{O}_2$
installing bulky pivalamide groups on one face of the porphyrin to sterically block formation of the bimolecular $\mu$-peroxo diiron intermediate
removing the proximal axial nitrogen ligand completely
questions.explanationEn: Irreversible autoxidation of unhindered $\text{Fe(II)}$ porphyrins proceeds via a bimolecular $\mu$-peroxo intermediate $[(\text{Por})\text{Fe}-\text{O}-\text{O}-\text{Fe}(\text{Por})]$ that cleaves to $\text{Fe}^{\text{IV}}=\text{O}$ and then forms the thermodynamic sink $[(\text{Por})\text{Fe}-\text{O}-\text{Fe}(\text{Por})]$. Collman's picket-fence porphyrin places four bulky pivalamide 'pickets' on one face (creating a steric pocket for small $\text{O}_2$ while blocking a second porphyrin from approaching) and a bulky imidazole on the opposite face.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the plot of nuclear binding energy per nucleon ($\text{BE}/A$) versus mass number ($A$), the curve rises sharply for light nuclei, peaks near $^{56}\text{Fe}$ ($\approx 8.8\text{ MeV/nucleon}$), and decreases gradually toward $^{238}\text{U}$ ($\approx 7.6\text{ MeV/nucleon}$). Which statement is a direct consequence of this curve?
optionsEn: $^{238}\text{U}$ has a higher binding energy per nucleon than $^{56}\text{Fe}$
Fusion of two $^{56}\text{Fe}$ nuclei is strongly exoergic

Both fusion of very light nuclei (e.g., $^2\text{H} + {}^3\text{H}$) and fission of very heavy nuclei (e.g., $^{235}\text{U}$) are exoergic because the products have higher binding energy per nucleon than the reactants
Fission of $^{56}\text{Fe}$ into two $^{28}\text{Al}$ nuclei releases large amounts of energy
questions.explanationEn: Energy is released whenever a nuclear reaction produces nuclei with a HIGHER binding energy per nucleon (more tightly bound, lower total mass). Moving toward the maximum at $^{56}\text{Fe}$ from the left (fusion of light nuclei) or from the right (fission of heavy nuclei like $^{235}\text{U}$) increases $\text{BE}/A$ and is therefore exoergic.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements regarding binary metal carbonyls are CORRECT?
optionsEn: $\text{V}(\text{CO})_6$ is a $17$-electron paramagnetic monomer that does NOT dimerize at room temperature due to steric crowding in a 7-coordinate dimer
In solid $\text{Fe}_2(\text{CO})_9$, there are three bridging $\mu_2\text{-CO}$ ligands, six terminal $\text{CO}$ ligands, and a formal $\text{Fe}-\text{Fe}$ single bond
In $\text{Mn}_2(\text{CO})_{10}$, all ten $\text{CO}$ ligands are terminal and the two $\text{Mn}(\text{CO})_5$ units adopt a staggered ($D_{4d}$) conformation
$\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_5$ is rigidly static on the $^{13}\text{C}$ NMR timescale at $25\,^\circ\text{C}$, showing two distinct $^{13}\text{C}$ signals in a $2:3$ ratio
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: $\text{V}(\text{CO})_6$ ($17\text{ e}^-$) resists dimerization because forming $\text{V}_2(\text{CO})_{12}$ would increase coordination number to $7$ with severe steric repulsion; instead it readily reduces to $[\text{V}(\text{CO})_6]^-$. (B) True: $\text{Fe}_2(\text{CO})_9$ ($D_{3h}$) has $3$ bridging COs, $6$ terminal COs, and $1$ $\text{Fe}-\text{Fe}$ bond ($36 - 34 = 2 \implies 1$ bond). (C) True: $\text{Mn}_2(\text{CO})_{10}$ has $D_{4d}$ symmetry with $0$ bridging COs. (D) False: $\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_5$ undergoes rapid Berry pseudorotation at $25\,^\circ\text{C}$, showing only ONE $^{13}\text{C}$ NMR singlet. Hence (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Regarding migratory insertion of $\text{CO}$ into an $\text{M}-\text{R}$ bond in octahedral complexes such as $[\text{Mn}(\text{CH}_3)(\text{CO})_5] + \text{L} \to [\text{Mn}(\text{COCH}_3)(\text{CO})_4\text{L}]$, which statements are CORRECT?
optionsEn: The $\text{CH}_3$ group migrates to an adjacent *cis*-$\text{CO}$ ligand, and the incoming ligand $\text{L}$ enters *cis* to the newly formed acyl group
When an optically active chiral alkyl group $\text{R}^*$ migrates onto $\text{CO}$, migration proceeds with RETENTION of configuration at the migrating carbon center
Lewis acids (such as $\text{AlCl}_3$ or $\text{Li}^+$) accelerate migratory insertion by coordinating to the acyl oxygen and stabilizing the transition state
Migratory insertion of $\text{CO}$ can occur directly with a *trans*-$\text{CO}$ ligand without isomerization
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: $^{13}\text{CO}$ labeling studies by Calderazzo and Noack proved alkyl migration onto a *cis*-$\text{CO}$ with $\text{L}$ trapping the vacated *cis* site. (B) True: concerted $1,2$-migration preserves stereochemical configuration at the $\alpha$-carbon (retention). (C) True: Lewis acids bind the developing negative charge on the acyl oxygen, lowering the activation barrier. (D) False: the migrating alkyl and $\text{CO}$ MUST be mutually *cis*. Hence (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements regarding Mössbauer spectroscopy and thermal analysis (TGA/DTA/DSC) are CORRECT?
optionsEn: In a $^{57}\text{Fe}$ Mössbauer spectrum, an internal or external magnetic field splits the nuclear transition into a $6$-line hyperfine sextet (governed by $\Delta m_I = 0, \pm 1$)

In $\text{Fe}_3(\text{CO})_{12}$, $^{57}\text{Fe}$ Mössbauer spectroscopy reveals two distinct iron environments (a quadrupole doublet for the two bridged $\text{Fe}$ atoms and a singlet/narrow doublet for the unique apical $\text{Fe}$ atom) in a $2:1$ area ratio
In DTA and DSC, an endothermic process (such as melting or dehydration) and an exothermic process (such as crystallization or oxidation) produce peaks in opposite directions relative to the baseline
TGA can detect solid-solid polymorphic phase transitions that involve no change in chemical composition
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: magnetic Zeeman splitting lifts $I=1/2$ into $2$ levels and $I=3/2$ into $4$ levels; selection rule $\Delta m_I = 0, \pm 1$ allows $6$ transitions (sextet). (B) True: $\text{Fe}_3(\text{CO})_{12}$ has $2$ symmetry-equivalent CO-bridged Fe centers (large $\Delta E_Q$) and $1$ unique apical Fe center (near-zero $\Delta E_Q$), giving a $2:1$ area ratio. (C) True: endothermic and exothermic thermal events produce opposite-sign peaks in DTA/DSC. (D) False: polymorphic phase transitions involve zero mass change and are invisible in TGA (detected by DTA/DSC). Hence (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the $18$-electron tungsten dicarbonyl complex $[(\eta^x\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5)(\eta^y\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5)\text{W}(\text{CO})_2]$ (atomic number of $\text{W} = 74$), the two cyclopentadienyl rings exhibit different hapticities. The sum $x + y$ is _______ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Using the neutral-ligand method, $\text{W}$ (Group 6) contributes $6\text{ e}^-$ and two $\text{CO}$ ligands contribute $2 \times 2 = 4\text{ e}^-$, totaling $10\text{ e}^-$. To satisfy the $18$-electron rule, the two $\text{C}_5\text{H}_5$ ligands together must donate $18 - 10 = 8\text{ e}^-$. Since an $\eta^k\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5$ ligand donates $k$ electrons in the neutral method, $x + y = 8$ (specifically $\eta^5$ and $\eta^3$, i.e., $5 + 3 = 8$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organometallic, Bioinorganic & Nuclear Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For the $\alpha$-decay $^{226}_{88}\text{Ra} \longrightarrow {}^{222}_{86}\text{Rn} + {}^{4}_{2}\text{He}$, the exact atomic masses are $m(^{226}\text{Ra}) = 226.025410\text{ u}$, $m(^{222}\text{Rn}) = 222.017578\text{ u}$, and $m(^{4}\text{He}) = 4.002603\text{ u}$. Taking $1\text{ u} = 931.5\text{ MeV}$, the $Q$-value of this decay (in $\text{MeV}$, rounded off to two decimal places) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: The mass defect is $\Delta m = m(^{226}\text{Ra}) - [m(^{222}\text{Rn}) + m(^{4}\text{He})] = 226.025410 - (222.017578 + 4.002603) = 0.005229\text{ u}$. Multiplying by $931.5\text{ MeV u}^{-1}$ yields $Q = 0.005229 \times 931.5 = 4.8708 \approx 4.87\text{ MeV}$.
